title: Radar echoes from Venus, Millstone, spring 1961 (Pettengill et al. 1962, Tables I-III, our transcription), reduced again with JPL DE440 into the astronomical unit

radius_enters_via.how: the antenna's offset from the Earth's centre on the International Ellipsoid (up to 6,378 km on 42-67 million km)
JPL DE440, whose orbits rest in part on later radar ranging

verdict_rule: Echoes coming back in a fraction of a second (a Venus a few thousand km away), or flight times that no single astronomical unit fits over the two months (the orbits' shape in AU wrong).
license_note: The 1962 article (Astron. J., NASA ADS scan) is cited and its tables transcribed as data; JPL DE440, public.

sources.cite: G. H. Pettengill, H. W. Briscoe, J. V. Evans, E. Gehrels, G. M. Hyde, L. G. Kraft, R. Price and W. B. Smith, A Radar Investigation of Venus, Astron. J. 67 (1962) 181-190, Tables I (p. 182), II (p. 183) and III (p. 186)
R. S. Park, W. M. Folkner, J. G. Williams and D. H. Boggs, The JPL Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides DE440 and DE441, Astron. J. 161 (2021) 105

units.ut: UT of the instant of reflection at Venus, as printed
units.delay: s, observed two-way echo flight time, as printed
units.au_newcomb, au_duncombe, err: km, the authors' reductions and measurement error, as printed (the leading 149 restored)

inputs.origin: Pettengill et al., Astron. J. 67 (1962) 181-190, Tables I (p. 182), II (p. 183) and III (p. 186), NASA ADS scan; typed by hand by the assistant (Claude) from the scans, under Xyphophor's review.
inputs.checks: The build recomputes the printed astronomical units from the transcribed flight times and fails on a disagreement.

notes: DE440 is the file of moon-eclcraters (data/moon/eclcraters/raw/de440.bsp, fog fetch moon-eclcraters), not downloaded twice. Method and references: go doc -all ./internal/build/orbradar.
